description: Bubble Shooter online free: aim the cannon, match three or more bubbles of a colour to pop them, and clear the board before it crosses the red line.
lede: The casual classic, in your browser. A board full of glossy coloured bubbles hangs from the top of the screen, and your cannon sits at the bottom, loaded and ready. Aim, shoot, and match three or more of a colour to pop them — and watch the bubbles left hanging drop away for bonus points. Clear the whole board to reach the next level, but beware: every few shots that pop nothing drops the ceiling a row closer to the red line.

p: Press Start popping and a board of coloured bubbles appears, five rows deep. Drag your finger or mouse across the board to aim the cannon — a dotted line shows where your bubble will fly, including one bounce off the side wall — then release to shoot. Your bubble sticks to the board where it lands.

Match three or more bubbles of the same colour and they pop for 10 points each. Bubbles left hanging with nothing above them drop away too, worth 10 points each as well. Clear every bubble on the board to finish the level: you earn a bonus and a fresh board appears, a little deeper and, from level three, with a fifth colour. But every six shots that pop nothing drop the whole ceiling one row lower, and if any bubble crosses the red line, the game is over.

Every bubble you pop is worth 10 points, and a group of five or more earns a 50-point bonus on top. Bubbles that drop because they lost their support are worth 10 points each too, so a well-placed shot that cuts a whole cluster loose can be worth far more than the three bubbles it popped.

Clearing a level pays 150 points plus 50 per level, so the level-one bonus is 200. Level one starts with five rows and four colours; level three adds a sixth row and a fifth colour, purple. The ceiling drop comes every six shots that pop nothing, so steady popping keeps the board high.

sections.h: From the arcade to the browser
p: Bubble shooters began with Puzzle Bobble, released by Taito in 1994 as Bust-A-Move outside Japan. Two little bubble dragons fired coloured bubbles at a board, and matching three popped them — the same rule this game uses. The dragons, Bubblun and Bobblun, were already famous from Taito's Bubble Bobble, the 1986 arcade game where they trapped enemies in bubbles and popped them.

A decade later the idea moved to the web, where a simple mouse-aimed Bubble Shooter became one of the most played casual games of the 2000s. No lives, no timer, just aim and pop — the formula has barely changed since, because it never needed to. The version here keeps the classic rules: four colours to start, a fifth from level three, and a ceiling that drops when you stop popping.

ol: Aim for the bottom of a cluster, not the top. Popping the lowest bubbles in a group cuts everything above them loose, and dropped bubbles score just as much as popped ones.
Use the walls. A bubble bounces off the side wall once, so an angled shot can reach a colour hiding behind a column you cannot hit straight on.
Follow the dotted line. It shows the bounce and stops where your bubble will land, so you can check a tricky shot before you commit to it.
Save your colours. The cannon always loads a colour that is still on the board, and the next bubble is shown beside the cannon — plan two shots ahead, not one.
Clear one colour completely when you can. With fewer colours on the board, the cannon loads the colours you need more often.
On a phone, drag with one thumb to aim and tap SHOOT with the other. The cannon follows your finger, so you can keep adjusting right up to the shot.

p: For another one-more-go classic, smash the bricks in [[breakout]] or slice the fruit in [[fruit-slice]]. If you would rather test your memory than your aim, repeat the pattern in [[simon-says]]. You can find every fast, one-more-go game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: How many bubbles do I need to match?
Three or more of the same colour, touching each other. A pair will not pop — the bubble just sticks to the board.
What happens to bubbles left hanging?
They drop away. Any bubble that is no longer connected to the ceiling falls off the board, worth 10 points each, the moment your shot resolves.
After every six shots that pop nothing. Shots that pop bubbles reset the count, so steady popping keeps the board high. The countdown is shown at the top as Drop in.
Can I bounce shots off the walls?
Yes. A bubble bounces off the left and right walls once, and the dotted aim line shows the bounce, so you can reach colours hiding behind other bubbles.
What happens if the bubbles cross the red line?
The game ends at once. The red dashed line near the bottom is the last line of defence — any bubble touching it ends the game, even on a level you were about to clear.
Four at first: red, blue, green and yellow. From level three a fifth colour, purple, joins the board, and the board starts one row deeper.
Yes. Your best score is saved in this browser on this device, and it is shown at the top of the screen and on the start card.
